citation: Olanrewaju-George B, Pranggono B. Federated learning-based intrusion detection system for the internet of things using unsupervised and supervised deep learning models. Cyber Security and Applications 3:100068, 2025. doi:10.1016/j.csa.2024.100068

A1.evidence: Sec 3.3: "a random sample of the abnormal data is created and concatenated with the normal testing set... They are shuffled"; percentages not given.

A2.evidence: Sec 4.1: AE and DNN take the 115 features of a record as input; no windows/sequences.

A3.evidence: Sec 3.3: "the normal training set, the normal threshold set, and the mixed data are scaled using a scaler function" - what the scaler is fitted on is not stated.

A4.evidence: Tables 2-3 give (per-device) epochs from random search; number of FL rounds not stated ("repeated until the global AE model converges").

A5.evidence: Table 4: "Performance comparison ... with other studies that used N-BaIoT dataset" with values cited from [6],[7],[8],[11],[12],[14].

A6.evidence: Table 4 baseline numbers quoted from other papers; Table 5 ML models and Non-FL models (Figs 5-7) also compared, with no stated training details.

A7.evidence: Sec 4.4: "accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score" plus TPR/FPR; no MCC/balanced accuracy.

A8.evidence: "Each IoT device trains an AE locally on its data"; nine N-BaIoT devices as clients (natural split); no non-IID partition evaluated.

A9.evidence: No repeated runs or dispersion reported.

A11.evidence: Only dataset link (UCI) given; no code link.

notes: Clients = nine N-BaIoT devices (natural per-device split). Unclear whether Table 2-3 epochs are FL local epochs. Mixed baselines: literature numbers (Table 4) and ML models (Table 5) of unstated provenance; coded copied because some are copied.
